title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Threatening Quasi-Criminal Proceedings
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal is trying to collect a civil debt of $4,000 for their client. The paralegal sends a demand letter to the opposing party stating, "If you do not pay this debt within 7 days, my client will report your business practices to the police to have criminal fraud charges laid." Is this ethically permissible?
options: Yes, if the paralegal genuinely believes the opposing party committed fraud.
Yes, a demand letter is a protected communication in the course of litigation.
No, it is professional misconduct to threaten criminal or quasi-criminal proceedings to gain a civil advantage.
No, unless the paralegal includes a draft of the police report with the demand letter.
questions.explain: Under Rule 2.02, a paralegal shall not, in an attempt to gain a benefit for a client, threaten, or advise a client to threaten, to initiate or proceed with a charge for an offence, including an offence under the Criminal Code or a provincial statute.
